sections.html:
Yamhill County's biggest city and its seat, McMinnville stands in the Willamette Valley below the Oregon Coast Range, beside the point where two forks of the Yamhill River join. Portland is about 37 miles northeast and Salem about 26 miles southeast. The city covers 10.58 square miles at 161 feet above sea level.

Downtown runs along East Third Street, older residential streets spread west along West Second Street, and Baker Creek Road and Cypress Street tie the outer residential and industrial areas together. Buyers shop a west-side house very differently from one near the highway corridor, so your street counts as much as the town.

Residents numbered 34,319 in 2020, against 32,187 in 2010 and 26,499 in 2000, with 34,647 estimated for July 1, 2025. Housing totaled 13,257 units in 2020, and owners occupied 59.5 percent.

Federal survey estimates for 2020 to 2024 show a city where most households own. They describe the whole city and say nothing about the price of one house.

Housing measure, 2020 to 2024McMinnville
Owner-occupied housing unit rate62.9%
Median value of owner-occupied units$432,800
Median gross rent$1,380
Households12,795
Persons per household2.54

Use the median value only as background. Your house will be priced by its condition, street and size, and a cash offer will reflect the repairs it needs. With one resident in five aged 65 or older, downsizing and inherited houses show up regularly among local sales.

Health care, higher education and manufacturing anchor the job base. Willamette Valley Medical Center, Linfield University and Cascade Steel Rolling Mills lead the local employer list. Linfield enrolls about 2,000 students on nearly 200 acres, and its students and staff add to local rental and housing demand.

Wine adds another layer. The McMinnville AVA was established in January 2005 and covers 14 wineries and 523 acres within the Willamette Valley AVA, and Yamhill County has the largest vineyard area of any Oregon county. A seller whose house sits near vineyard land or the downtown tasting rooms is selling into that setting, so mention it.

Summers are warm and the wet season is long. Mean temperatures by month run from 40.5 degrees in December to 67.5 degrees in August, and rain averages 37.64 inches a year with November the wettest month. The record high is 114 degrees, set June 28, 2021, and marine fog from the coast is common.

Months of damp work on roofs, gutters, siding and crawl spaces, and you should inspect them before a buyer's inspector does. For a large repair, collect more than one quote.

Oregon Route 99W runs through the city, Oregon Route 18 bypasses it to the south and leads to the coast, and Route 47 begins just northeast of the city limits. Newberg and Portland are reachable along 99W, which matters to commuters. Public transit comes from the Yamhill County Transit Area, and freight rail has run through the city on the Portland & Western Railroad since 1993.

Public schooling is handled by the McMinnville School District, which has about 7,000 students, five elementary schools, two middle schools and McMinnville High School. Private choices include McMinnville Montessori School, McMinnville Christian Academy and St. James Catholic Elementary School. Ask the district about attendance boundaries before claiming a particular school for your house.

McMinnville Water and Light, a city-owned utility, handles electric and water service. Its main office is at 340 NE Kirby Street, and the phone number is (503) 472-6158. Call to set a final meter reading and a date to transfer service. Residential sewer charges are based on water use from November through March, so the final bill may reflect your winter use. Mention that to the buyer so there is no confusion over who owes what.

The county tax office in Yamhill County sends the bill, which Oregon lets you pay in three installments on November 15, February 15 and May 15. A full payment by November 15 takes 3% off, and two-thirds by then takes 2% off.

Interest of 1 1/3% a month builds on late amounts, beginning after December 15 for the first installment. ORS 308.146 generally holds taxable value growth to 3% a year unless the property changes, which is why a buyer's bill may not match yours. The title company will split the current year's tax at closing.

sections.h2: What a McMinnville seller must disclose
sections.html:
Anyone selling a one-to-four-unit home in Oregon usually signs a seller's property disclosure statement for each buyer who offers in writing. That buyer then has five business days to revoke, unless a written waiver came first.

Under ORS 105.470 some sellers are exempt, such as court-appointed personal representatives, trustees and financial institutions that took the property through foreclosure. Handling an inherited house? Ask the estate's attorney if the exemption fits.

A short checklist keeps a McMinnville sale on schedule. Ask the title company for a payoff figure covering your mortgage and any open tax installment. Call McMinnville Water and Light to line up the final reading. If the house is an estate property, have the attorney confirm who can sign and whether the disclosure exemption applies.

Then look at the calendar. Installment dates, a move-out day and the buyer's closing date should not collide. Raise any conflict with the buyer early, since most can be solved by moving a signing date a few days.

Local sellers tend to weigh three paths: an agent listing, a sale without an agent, or an as-is offer from a cash buyer. Each buyer sets its own terms and timeline, so look past the headline number.

  • Condition: wet-season roof, gutter and crawl-space wear is common in older houses.
  • Timing: tax installments, utility transfer and any move-out date.
  • Paperwork: the disclosure statement, or the estate exclusion if it applies.
  • Costs: who pays for repairs, title and closing.

Offers on rough houses are realistic here, though the price will account for repairs. No lender signs off on a cash deal, so the closing date comes from you and the title company. Yamhill County records the deed, and a mortgage payoff or unpaid tax is taken from what you receive.

We buy houses in McMinnville as they are. Ask for an offer online or by phone, then weigh the written number against the cost of repairs, commissions and months of mortgage payments on a listing.

faqs.q: How many people live in McMinnville?
faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 34,647 residents. The 2020 census counted 34,319.

faqs.q: When are Oregon property taxes due?
faqs.a: The three installments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15. A 3% discount applies if you pay in full by November 15.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a disclosure statement when I sell in McMinnville?
faqs.a: Usually yes for a one-to-four-unit home, with exclusions such as court-appointed sellers and foreclosing financial institutions. A buyer who gets the statement has five business days to revoke the offer unless they waived that right.

faqs.q: Who do I call to stop utilities when I sell?
faqs.a: Call McMinnville Water and Light at (503) 472-6158 to schedule a final reading and transfer of service.

faqs.q: Can I sell a McMinnville house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Yes. Cash buyers and some regular buyers will take a house in any condition, though the offer will reflect the repairs. Collect more than one opinion on the work needed.
